label: map_1
name: One-way pykrete flood barges
mech: In winter, shallow moulds on the frozen banks of a river near the mine are flooded with river water mixed with sawdust, and the cold freezes them into thick pykrete hulls. Ore concentrate is sealed inside these hulls in waterproof bags. At spring breakup the hulls float free and ride the flood hundreds of kilometres downstream to an Arctic port or rail point. There the cargo is lifted out and the hull is simply left to melt. A short GPS and ice-thickness log for each hull is used to adjust next year's hull thickness and launch dates to the river's real flood behaviour.
value: Bulk cargo can leave roadless deposits once a year with no steel fleet, no return trips and no road, using a free current and a hull that costs almost nothing.

label: map_1
name: Frost-wedge in-situ ore shattering
mech: In autumn, a dense grid of cheap boreholes is drilled into the ore body and flooded with water. Winter air is then blown or naturally drawn through them, so the water freezes and expands by about 9%. Repeated over several freeze-thaw cycles, this splits the rock along its grain boundaries into fine fragments. Temperature and acoustic sensors in the boreholes record where cracking has slowed, and the next year's water injection is concentrated in those zones. In the thaw season the fines are washed or vacuumed out instead of being blasted and crushed.
value: Most of the cost of blasting, explosives transport and crushing disappears, because the Arctic climate breaks the rock for free.

label: map_1
name: Winter freeze-concentration of leachates
mech: A dilute leach solution or brine carrying metals or rare earths is sprayed or spread in thin layers over a sloped field during winter. Freezing pushes the dissolved salts out of the pure ice, and the concentrated liquid drains away into collecting channels. The spraying rate and the number of passes are adjusted from conductivity readings at the outlet until the target concentration is reached. The ice left behind is nearly clean water that is reused in spring.
value: Concentrating metals before shipping, normally an energy-hungry step, becomes nearly free, so only a small volume of high-grade liquor has to leave the site.

label: map_3
name: Grown pykrete drift barges
mech: In winter, crews repeatedly flood thin layers of river water mixed with wood-chip waste onto riverbank ice. This builds pykrete slabs about 100x30x5 m, each able to float roughly 1,000 t of bagged ore concentrate. The cargo is loaded on top while everything is frozen. At spring breakup the slab floats free, and small tugs steer it down the Lena or Yenisei to an Arctic transshipment port. There it is unloaded and left to melt, so no barge has to go back upstream.
value: Each spring flood becomes a one-way bulk fleet whose only materials are water, sawdust and frost.

label: map_3
name: Cable-hauled ice guideway sleds
mech: Sprinkler rigs build a narrow, graded ice trough along a fixed line from a deposit to a railhead or river. They refresh it automatically whenever the temperature drops enough. Steel-runner ore sleds clip onto an endless steel cable loop, like a ski lift, driven by motors at the two ends. Because runners on ice have friction close to rail, a single loop moves a continuous stream of cargo without trucks, drivers or road surface. Sensors on the track trigger re-spraying wherever the ice wears down.
value: Gives near-railway freight costs every winter for the price of a cable, two winches and a water pump.

label: map_3
name: Permafrost-sealed in-place leaching
mech: Blasting breaks up the ore body underground, and circulating warm brine thaws only a bounded block of it. A leaching solution is then pumped through the block to dissolve the metal, and wells recover it. Any liquid that leaks toward the edge of the block refreezes on contact with the surrounding frozen ground, so the permafrost acts as a self-healing container. Temperature readings at the boundary show where the seal is. Only the recovered metal, often under 1% of the ore's mass, is ever transported.
value: Extracts metals from remote frozen deposits with no pit, no ore haulage and no artificial liner.
